info.description:
The ITMatrixHQ market analytics API. Every `/v2` response is a `{data, meta}` envelope; errors carry one code from a closed set; `meta.plane` reports provenance and `meta.caps` any entitlement limit that was applied.

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer itm_<key>`. The ITMatrixHQ apps send a first-party session token on the same header. An API key is refused with `403 not_entitled_tier` unless its account includes API access (web Pro includes API Explorer; the API plan includes API Pro), and with `403 attestation_required` unless the account has recorded a market-data classification. Index symbols (SPX, NDX, VIX and others) and options on them are refused to API keys with `403 not_entitled_symbol`: index data is available in the ITMatrixHQ apps only.

Requests with an API key are rate limited per account: all of an account's keys share one per-minute budget, set by its plan. Every keyed response carries `x-ratelimit-limit` (requests per minute), `x-ratelimit-remaining` and `x-ratelimit-reset` (Unix seconds at which the budget is full again). A request over the limit may be refused with `429 rate_limited` and a `Retry-After` header. `GET /v2/account/usage` reports the account's limit.

Tags are scope groups, operationIds are `<scopeGroup>_<verbNoun>`, and `x-exposure` marks each operation `public`, `app-only` or `internal`. API keys may call `public` operations only.

get.description:
Every listed contract of one underlying from a single capture, with quotes, open interest, implied volatility and greeks.

Read it live, or as of a past time with `at`. Every row is valued against the capture's one `spot`, and `partial: true` marks a capture known to be incomplete.

#### Units

- `oi` and `volume` are contracts; `theta` is dollars per day.
- `shares_per_contract` is the contract multiplier, 100 for standard contracts.

#### Freshness

A live chain is re-captured at most every 30 seconds per symbol, and may be up to 5 minutes old while a refresh runs. `captured_at` says when it was taken.

With an API key, a live chain's `spot` is the latest price from the ITMatrixHQ price engine at request time, or `null` when it has none.

#### Empty results

A symbol with no listed options returns `rows: []`.

#### Limits

A key may have 6 history reads in flight at once (14 on Pro), shared across stock bars, GEX session history and `at=` reads of the GEX grid and the option chain; a seventh (fifteenth on Pro) `at=` read gets `429 rate_limited`.

#### Example

One contract (`meta` truncated):


- GEX values are dollars of dealer hedging per $1 move in the underlying, calls positive and puts negative.
- Each `*_shares` field is its dollar sibling in shares of the underlying per $1 move: the dollar value divided by `spot`, or by `prior_close_spot` when `spot` is `null`.

A live read serves the latest capture, and a new capture lands every 5 minutes during market hours. Before the day's first capture, and on weekends and holidays, it serves the most recent session with data and names it in `meta.date`. get.description:
OHLCV bars for one stock over `[from, to)`, ascending, at one-second to daily resolution.

With an API key the finest resolution is five minutes: `1s` and `1m` are `400 invalid_params`, and an omitted `timeframe` is `5m`.

Page through a long range by repeating the request with `cursor` set to `meta.cursor` until it is absent. `meta.complete_through` is the last complete bar; the bar after it can still change.

#### Units

`volume` is shares. Prices are on the axis `meta.adjustment` names, with the last corporate action it accounts for: `split` (the default) rescales every bar to today's share count, and `adj=none` serves bars as traded. `meta.basis` names the price source and `meta.coverage_end` whether a daily bar ends at the regular close (`rth`) or the extended one (`extended`). Bars of unequal basis are never stitched silently: `meta.seam` says where they meet, or which rows were left out.

#### Empty results

A real ticker with no bars in the range returns an empty `data` list. An unknown ticker is `404 not_found`.

#### Limits

With an API key the minimum `timeframe` is `5m`: `5m`, `1h` and `1d` are served, and `1s` or `1m` is `400 invalid_params`.

Requests with an API key get at most 1,000 bars per page and a span of at most 30 days at `5m`, 90 days at `1h` or 2 years at `1d`. A longer span or larger `limit` is clamped, and `meta.caps.applied` lists `range_clamped` or `limit_clamped`. A key may have 6 history reads in flight at once (14 on Pro), shared across stock bars, GEX session history and `at=` reads of the GEX grid and the option chain; a seventh (fifteenth on Pro) gets `429 rate_limited`.

#### Example

Two daily bars (`data` and `meta` truncated):

```http
GET /v2/stocks/SPY/bars?timeframe=1d&from=2026-09-21&to=2026-09-26
```

```json

    {
      "symbol": "SPY",
      "timeframe": "1d",
      "ts_ms": 1790035200000,
      "open": 774.03,
      "high": 775.14,
      "low": 772.57,
      "close": 773.38,
      "volume": 34802336,
      "trade_count": 470399
    },
    {
      "symbol": "SPY",
      "timeframe": "1d",
      "ts_ms": 1790121600000,
      "open": 772.79,
      "high": 773.05,
      "low": 766.5,
      "close": 767.81,
      "volume": 54931688,
      "trade_count": 614754
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "caps": {
      "tier": "pro",
      "applied": []
    },
    "complete_through": 1790308800000,
    "row_count": 5
  }
}
```
